method:
Event study for the Momentum tab's crossover signals — the honest version.

Replaces the t-stat-vs-zero backtest retired 07-Sep-26. That version had two
flaws that manufactured "edge" out of nothing:
  1. it tested mean forward return against ZERO, so on assets that drifted for
     eleven years every bearish cross looked like a FADE and every bullish
     cross looked like edge (of 21 signals it badged HIGH, none survived once
     the unconditional drift was subtracted; in 91% of asset/signal pairs the
     bull cross and the bear cross had forward returns of the SAME sign);
  2. its Confluence signal used a two-sided +/-7 calendar-day window, i.e. it
     counted a date as confluence if a second signal fired the FOLLOWING week
     — the second cross only happens because price kept going, so the 1W
     return was baked into the selection (41 of 56 asset/directions at |t|>=2
     two-sided; 2 of 56 with a causal window).

What this does instead, per ticker, per signal, in BOTH directions always:
  * excess = mean forward return of the signal dates minus the unconditional
    mean over the same sample (drift removed)
  * p = placebo bootstrap: 2000 draws of n random dates from the same sample;
    one-sided in the stated direction. Fat tails and drift are in the placebo
    by construction.
  * Confluence is CAUSAL: >=2 of the three signals fired the same way within
    the PRIOR 7 calendar days; the confluence date is the later cross.
  * verdict at 1M: EDGE p<=0.025 & n>=15 · WEAK p<=0.10 · NONE otherwise.
    The file also reports how many tests were run and how many EDGE verdicts
    chance alone would produce, and the UI prints it — read the tab as
    context, not as an anchor. Setups no longer consumes it.
  * a trend-score study per ticker: forward 1M return by score band (from
    trend_engine) + rank IC, so the anchor's edge on THIS asset is visible.
